Pittsburgh isn't just dealing with the early NFL Injury pileup. But the TNF showdown marked the first game following the league's latest blockbuster trade.

fullText:
Going into a tough matchup against the Los Angeles Rams this weekend, the Philadelphia Eagles have a loaded injury report. The wide receiver DeVonta Smith is a headliner.

For the second straight week, Smith is dealing with a hamstring injury. On Wednesday, the Eagles had a walkthrough, but estimated that Smith would not practice at all if they held a session.

When the team returned to the field on Thursday for an actual practice session, Smith was absent. He was listed on the injury report as a non-participant.

While Smith's lingering hamstring issue forced him to miss some practice before Week 3 against the Chicago Bears, a game he played in, this time seems different.

"There is not much optimism Eagles receiver DeVonta Smith will play Sunday against the Rams," ESPN's Tim McManus reported after Thursday's practice.

"Smith has been sidelined with a hamstring injury this week and the expectation is he won't be able to go Sunday."

If true, that's a brutal blow for Philadelphia's offense, after they just spent a game struggling with Smith on the field. In the loss, Smith was targeted eight times. He caught six passes for 65 yards.

The Eagles were dominated by the Bears, taking on a 27-7 loss.

In addition to Smith, the Eagles will more than likely be without the veteran tight end Dallas Goedert. After Goedert suffered a knee injury in Week 2, the Eagles expect him to be ruled out for multiple weeks.

The passing game will rely on guys like Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, and Zach Ertz to step up. Dairus Cooper and the injured Hollywood Brown (if he plays) could be in line for more snaps as well.

The Eagles will host the Rams on Sunday, October 4.

title: New biography on Ralph Wilson released
description: BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) — D’Youville University hosted the release of sports historian Greg Tranter’s newest book on Thursday, ‘Ralph C. Wilson Jr., The Conscience of the NFL.
fullText:
BUFFALO, N.Y. (WIVB) -- D'Youville University hosted the release of sports historian Greg Tranter's newest book on Thursday, 'Ralph C. Wilson Jr., The Conscience of the NFL.'

The biography explores the influence of the late owner of the Buffalo Bills across 50 years in the NFL, as well as his business ventures, philanthropy, and service in World War II.

Tranter said that fans of the Bills will be fans of his book.

"It's the history of the team through his eyes, so I think they'll really like that," Tranter said. "I think they'll learn things about him that people don't know, like his military history; he was a naval guy for World War II, he spent five years in the Navy, and there's some great stories about him in the Navy, so I think they'll appreciate all that."

The book is officially on sale in local bookstores and online.

title: Week 4 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Fantasy Wide Receivers
description: Welcome back, readers!
fullText:
Welcome back, readers! I am happy to return for a second year as The Sporting Tribune's fantasy football analyst. If you are new here, my mission is to help fantasy managers with any dilemmas or questions they may have through the course of the season to ultimately win their leagues. For the next 17 weeks, I will produce weekly fantasy content that will go over the waiver wire, rankings, and Start 'Em, Sit 'Em columns.

Being a fantasy manager often means having to make difficult roster decisions, but I aim to take some of the guesswork out of it with my Start 'Em and Sit 'Em column for every position. It goes without saying that I won't include obvious calls like "start Trey McBride" or "sit Tommy DeVito." Instead, I search for players that could be perceived as fringe that could propel your lineups for weekly wins.

As always, if you have any questions or don't see your players here, feel free to follow me on Twitter (X) – @JamesNewell96 and send me a message, where I typically respond in a timely manner.

Josh Downs vs. WSH (Projected FPTS – 13.9): Downs has been the beneficiary of Alec Pierce's absence, recording at least five catches and 70 receiving yards in back-to-back weeks. He's totaled 20 targets and scored 26.9 fantasy points. Expect him to be heavily involved in the Colts' game plan in Week Four against the Commanders. Washington's pass defense has lacked consistency, allowing 14-plus fantasy points to four opposing wide receivers through its first three games. The Commanders have also allowed the sixth-most fantasy points to slot receivers this season, which is where Downs lines up on most of his snaps.

Michael Wilson @ NYG (Projected FPTS – 13.3): Wilson put up a stellar performance in Week Three that looked reminiscent of his fantasy-league-winning stretch from last season. In the team's loss to the Niners, Wilson caught 11 of 17 targets and finished as the WR4 with 25.9 fantasy points. One interesting note: the only wideouts with more targets than Wilson are Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Chris Olave. He has a juicy matchup against the Giants in Week Four. With Wilson lining up outside on 78 percent of his snaps, New York's secondary has given up the sixth-most yards to outside receivers. Expect another big performance from the four-year veteran.

Tetairoa McMillan vs. DET (Projected FPTS – 15.3): Fantasy managers can admit that McMillan has been a bit underwhelming through the first three weeks, recording just one finish with over 10 fantasy points and currently sitting as the WR37. Nonetheless, the reigning Rookie of the Year should still be started without hesitation. He'll face the Lions in Week Four, who have one of the worst secondaries in the league. Detroit has allowed three wideouts to eclipse 19 fantasy points, and the team has surrendered the fourth-most receptions and yards, and fifth-most fantasy points per game, to opposing receivers.

Honorable Mentions: Keenan Allen @ WSH; Parker Washington @ CIN; Devaughn Vele vs. ATL; Malik Nabers vs. ARI; Matthew Golden @ TB; Luther Burden III vs. NYJ; Stefon Diggs @ IND; Deebo Samuel Sr. vs. DEN.

Ladd McConkey @ SEA (Projected FPTS – 12.3): McConkey being on my sit list may come as a surprise, but he's had an up-and-down start through the first three games. He's scored 10 or fewer points in each of his last two games and has been targeted just eight times during that span. I don't imagine fantasy managers benching McConkey, but keep in mind he's going against the Seahawks' secondary. They've allowed the fourth-fewest fantasy points to receivers and the seventh-fewest to slot receivers. The lone receiving touchdown Seattle has allowed this season came from Terry McLaurin last week.

Emeka Egbuka vs. GB (Projected FPTS – 10.6): Egbuka hasn't had any luck recapturing the ceiling he showed early in his rookie season. He's strung together double-digit fantasy point performances in all his games this season, but just by a slim margin. He'll enter Week Four without Baker Mayfield under center, who'll be out for at least the next two to four weeks. The Buccaneers will start undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback. Expect Egbuka's floor to take a dip against the Packers.

Jameson Williams @ CAR (Projected FPTS – 10.9): Williams has been "mid" through the first three weeks and is coming off an 8.9-fantasy-point outing against the Jets last week. He's averaged 7.6 fantasy points per game and has been targeted just four times in each of the last two games. One note about Williams: he's run 106 routes this season but has just a 16 percent target rate and is averaging 1.2 yards per route run. On paper, he has a tough matchup against the Panthers in Week Four, but Carolina will be without its two top corners, Jaycee Horn and Mike Jackson. There's a chance Williams finally has an explosive game, but I need to see it happen before starting him.

title: Former Steelers Linebacker Calls Out Patrick Queen: ‘Making Business Decisions’
description: Former Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Vince Williams did not hold back on Patrick Queen. Williams thinks Queen is making some business […]
fullText:
Former Pittsburgh Steelers linebacker Vince Williams did not hold back on Patrick Queen. Williams thinks Queen is making some business decisions in Thursday night's game against the Cleveland Browns.

"I'm a Queen fan but he's making business decisions out there. He knows this is his last year with the Steelers and he's playing safe," Williams wrote on X.

I'm a Queen fan but he's making business decisions out there. He knows this is his last year with the Steelers and he's playing safe.

— Vince Williams (@VinnyVidiVici98) October 2, 2026

It appears Williams is referring to the play below. Queen was hesitant to make a tackle on Browns running back Quinshon Judkins late in the first half. Deshaun Watson capped the drive with a 2-yard touchdown pass to Harold Fannin Jr. to give the Browns a 21-7 lead.

Watch Patrick Queen here. Sees Judkins with the ball and pretends to get blocked by Boston, who isn't even trying to block him, instead of running to the football. pic.twitter.com/n2euZ3N5dw

— Josh Rowntree (@JRown32) October 2, 2026

To say the least, Queen has had a rough game. He displayed poor effort on Jaleel McLaughlin's 28-yard touchdown run in the first quarter as well.

Jaleel McLaughlin just kept going for the touchdown!@PITvsCLE on Prime Video
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cvOr3FNWbx

Rounding into the last of his three-year contract, Queen's future with the Steelers is uncertain, but Queen will worry about that bridge when they come to it.

"(There) was talks here and there, nothing crazy," Queen said after an OTA's practice in May. "Obviously, I've seen the whole charade that went on over this offseason, but (there's) talks. Obviously, no movement, either way, and at the end of the day, they've got business to handle, I've got business to handle, and my business is to go out there and play the best football I can and put myself in a good position, put our team in a good position, so we can both can be successful."

Queen stacked up 126 total tackles last season, second on the team only to Payton Wilson. Queen was linked to the Dallas Cowboys in trade rumors earlier this offseason, but Jerry Jones' team wound up acquiring Dee Winters from the San Francisco 49ers.

"Some of it was true, some it was just extended truth," Queen said. "Just people rambling and stuff. That's what you're gonna have with social media nowadays, everybody wants the first say-so of whatever happens and they wanna hope to be right. But (there) was very slim facts out there, and that's all I'll leave it at."

Queen is making $10.83 million in base salary this season. He received a $2.5 million bonus on the third league day of 2026.

"I've got a good amount of money coming in this year, so at the end of the day I could care less," Queen said. "If they do wanna extend, cool. If not, cool. … The better I play, the better we both can be, so at that end of the day, that's all I care about."

Queen signed a three-year, $41 million contract with the Steelers in March of 2024.

title: Who is Devon Levi? Why Oilers Are Starting Rookie Against Canucks
description: Who is Devon Levi? Why are the Edmonton Oilers starting this rookie goaltender against the Vancouver Canucks? The post Who is Devon Levi? Why Oilers Are Starting Rookie Against Canucks appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
While the Edmonton Oilers figure out exactly what they want to do with Tristan Jarry, they will look at Devon Levi.

Before taking on the Vancouver Canucks, the Oilers announced a few moves involving Zach Hyman, Ryan Nugent-Hopkins, and Josh Samanski. They also announced their starting goaltender for tonight's game.

"Devon Levi will make his first start of the season as the #Oilers take on the Canucks in Vancouver," the team announced in a social media post, despite Bob Stauffer reporting it earlier in the day.

Devon Levi will make his first start of the season as the #Oilers take on the Canucks in Vancouver. @PlayAlbertaCA | #LetsGoOilers pic.twitter.com/ExnzHaNrU7

— Edmonton Oilers (@EdmontonOilers) October 1, 2026

That said, who exactly is Levi, and why is he the Oilers' starting goalie against the Canucks?

Oilers Trade Pitch Adds Connor Hellebuyck, Dumping $26 Million Burden

Levi is a 24-year-old goaltender who was acquired from the Buffalo Sabres this past summer in exchange for a third-round pick (the Oilers also picked up a seventh-round draft pick). He was originally drafted by the Florida Panthers, but was sent to Buffalo in the Sam Reinhart trade.

Levi has 39 games of NHL experience. In those games, he owns a 17-17-2 record, along with a 3.29 goals against average (GAA), and an .894 save percentage (SV%).

He is in the final year of a two-year, $1.63 million contract that he signed while with the Sabres.

Tristan Jarry got the nod for the Oilers in game one of the season. Unfortunately, that gloriously backfired in everyone's face.

Now, the youngster Levi gets his kick at the can.

At this point in the season, the team wants to see what they have. They would also love to see how Levi handles pressure this early in the season.

But Jarry has a very short leash, especially considering that he lost the starter's job to the now-retired Connor Ingram last season.

Before tending the twine for the first time in Oilers threads, Levi spoke about the opportunity of playing for a Stanley Cup contender.

"As a goalie … you want to be on a contender and you want to be the guy," Levi said via Sportsnet's Marc Spector. "All that being said, the focus here today is just to have fun, be present. I'm not looking at the end of the year and to win (the No. 1 job) today. Just let's see how I can put one block down to build a foundation for the end of the year."

At any rate, Levi is demonstrating that he has the head on his shoulders to bear the weight of the Oilers fanbase on his shoulders.

One way or another, he is going to have to do that in order to fully take advantage of this opportunity.

title: Columbus Fans Give Ex-Maple Leaf Matthew Knies Major 1st Impression
description: The Matthew Knies era with the Toronto Maple Leafs came to a close just days ago, as he was included in a blockbuster trade between Toronto and the Columbus Blue Jackets.Knies was dealt to the Blue Jackets along with forward Steven Lorentz, defenseman Emil Andrae, and a 2027 second-round draft pick; in return, Toronto received […] The post Columbus Fans Give Ex-Maple Leaf Matthew Knies Major 1st Impression appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Matthew Knies era with the Toronto Maple Leafs came to a close just days ago, as he was included in a blockbuster trade between Toronto and the Columbus Blue Jackets.

Knies was dealt to the Blue Jackets along with forward Steven Lorentz, defenseman Emil Andrae, and a 2027 second-round draft pick; in return, Toronto received forward Kirill Marchenko, goaltender Elvis Merzlikins (with 18 percent of his salary retained), and forward Miles Wood.

Neither Marchenko nor Knies had to wait long to make their debuts with their respective new clubs; Marchenko has already played two games in a Toronto jersey, and now Knies is getting his first crack with the Blue Jackets.

The Blue Jackets host the Buffalo Sabres at Nationwide Arena in what is the first regular season game of the 2026-27 NHL campaign for both sides.

When it came time for Knies' introduction, Blue Jackets fans immediately took kindly to their newest top-six forward, giving him a loud cheer.

Knies also walked the blue carpet along with his new teammates outside of the arena, signing autographs and taking selfies with fans.

Knies, who had been dealing with multiple trade rumors in recent weeks and months, is glad that he can put them all behind him and just focus on hockey now.

"I just kept coming up, and … it stuck with me, kind of hung over my head for a little bit," Knies said. "I'm fired up to go to Columbus and get a fresh start, a breath of fresh air and not have to worry about all that crap over my head, the trade stuff.

"I can just focus on hockey and focus on the guys in the room and try to win."

Meanwhile, he also said that he didn't realistically see a trade coming from the club that selected him.

"I really didn't see it happening," Knies said. "I thought it was going to happen sometime in the future, but, you know, not this quickly. It was kind of getting old here with all these rumors and stuff. I'm just glad that's put to bed, and I've got a new, fresh start in Columbus."

Knies, whom the Leafs took in the second round (57th overall pick) of the 2021 NHL Draft, joined the club after signing a three-year entry-level deal. He made his NHL debut soon afterward, playing in three regular-season contests before becoming part of Toronto's postseason roster.

Knies made an immediate impact in the playoffs, recording an assist on John Tavares' series-clinching goal against the Tampa Bay Lightning. The victory ended Toronto's long wait for a playoff series win, marking the franchise's first since 2004. Knies later scored his first NHL goal against the Florida Panthers in the second round, but his postseason came to an early end after he suffered a concussion.

The following season marked his first full NHL campaign, with Knies producing 15 goals and 20 assists. He took another step forward in 2024-25, setting a new career high with 29 goals.

title: ‘Save All the Theatrics’ — Super Bowl Champ Questions Aaron Rodgers’ ‘Rage Sessions’ at Steelers HC Mike McCarthy, Offers Simple Solution

fullText:
Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy were visibly frustrated with each other in the first half of the Pittsburgh Steelers' primetime matchup against their AFC North foe, the Cleveland Browns.

Rodgers was annoyed with McCarthy for not calling the play quickly, and McCarthy was angered by Rodgers's reaction. Amid a clear disconnect, former Super Bowl-winning OT Mitchell Schwartz offered a suggestion to avoid such spats.

Rodgers and McCarthy exchanged expletives and dirty looks over their disagreement. The= Steelers quarterback has expressed anger over certain play-calling decisions and had an episode today waiting for a play call.

Schwartz offered the solution that Rodgers can simply override the play call with one of his own if he is so disappointed in it.

"I still don't get why Rodgers doesn't just override McCarthy and call his own plays in certain situations," said Schwartz.

Quarterbacks have the freedom to audible out of certain play calls, but aren't usually calling plays themselves. Rodgers loves the chance to adjust things at the line to get the look he wants, but to do that, he needs the play call early, which is why he was annoyed.

When a fan countered that Schwartz is suggesting Rodgers is overriding certain plays and calling his own, Schwartz pointed to Rodgers's frequent displeasure with the playcalling.

This is Rodgers' final season in the NFL, and he is trying to go out with a bang. He's far from his MVP form and is the 30th-ranked quarterback in PFN's QB Impact Metric.

But he's trying to give what he's got left to get the Steelers a playoff win that has eluded them for a while now.

Rodgers needs to improve if the Steelers want to make a run this season. Whether that's with him calling plays or with McCarthy, the offense needs to be better.

title: Nets GM Marks Remaining Flexible With Trade Assets
description: Armed with thirteen first-round picks and massive future cap space, Sean Marks is hunting for a blockbuster superstar deal while cultivating a high-upside young core in Brooklyn.
fullText:
The Brooklyn Nets' greatest strength this season isn't veterans or youth; it's the 13 first-round picks.

General manager Sean Marks has accumulated hefty draft capital over the years by trading Kyrie Irving, Kevin Durant, James Harden, Cam Johnson and Mikal Bridges.

Marks has put Brooklyn in a position to operate with a "buyer's mentality" and make a blockbuster trade for a superstar. He tried to do this offseason, entering the Jaylen Brown sweepstakes, but the Boston Celtics dealt him to the Philadelphia 76ers.

The Nets' general manager is staying flexible with his assets. He's listening around the league for an opportunity that's worth pushing his chips in.

"It's also a combination of what becomes available," Marks told reporters at media day. "Can't predict when players from other teams become available or what free agency looks like down the road."

Teams have made unpredictable trades recently. The Dallas Mavericks traded superstar Luka Dončić to the Los Angeles Lakers for Anthony Davis last February; many thought Dončić would be a lifelong Maverick, much like franchise legend Dirk Nowitzki.

Brooklyn could also have over $60 million in cap space next offseason, and have no guaranteed money past the 2027-28 season. A clean slate like that sets the table for another active offseason.

The development of the Nets' young core also determines how fast or slow this rebuild is. Marks drafted Mikel Brown Jr., Joshua Jefferson and Tyler Bilodeau, adding them alongside the second-year Flatbush Five.

Egor Dëmin has shown the most improvement over the summer. He earned All-Summer League Second Team honors, showing improved downhill scoring, and has built a strong case for on-ball reps next season.

The rest — Nolan Traoré, Ben Saraf, Danny Wolf and Drake Powell — are competing for backup spots at their respective positions in training camp. If one of them makes a jump, then Brooklyn has a solid young core worth investing in.

Every year, the blueprint for building a championship team changes, but one rising trend is having valuable young players.

The Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs are the most recent examples. Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren are part of the Thunder's big three; Victor Wembanyama, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle are the Spurs' big three.

Brooklyn has the makings of a strong foundation, and it relies on how fast the young players develop. Patience is a virtue, but things can always change on the fly.

Marks can then capitalize on the growth of his young core by making a blockbuster trade when that idea is realized and a player he can use most of his assets to acquire becomes available.

title: Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy get into screaming match during Steelers-Browns game
description: On Sept. 20, the Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the New England Patriots by 17 points, and quarterback Aaron Rodgers delivered a backhanded assessment of head coach Mike McCarthy’s game plan. “In a game like today where there wasn’t a lot of flow to it, we need to be better, and it starts with me,” Rodgers…
fullText:
On Sept. 20, the Pittsburgh Steelers lost to the New England Patriots by 17 points, and quarterback Aaron Rodgers delivered a backhanded assessment of head coach Mike McCarthy's game plan.

"In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better, and it starts with me," Rodgers said. "Like, making sure that Mike knows what's working and what's not working. The coaches know, so that we can call stuff that gives us a better chance."

Pro Football Talk's Mike Florio described Rodgers's press conference comments as "passive-aggressive."

Well, what we saw during the Steelers' Thursday Night Football matchup with the Cleveland Browns was just aggressive-aggressive.

In the first quarter, the Prime Video broadcast caught Rodgers gesturing toward the Steelers sideline in apparent frustration over not getting the play in on time.

Aaron Rodgers: “WHAT THE F*CK?! CALL IT!”

Mike McCarthy: “F*cking a**hole.”pic.twitter.com/KOSwfYBL2J

— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 2, 2026

"He did this a lot during Cincinnati last week, kind of looking over to the bench," play-by-play legend Al Michaels said. As he said it, viewers could hear Rodgers screaming, "What the f*ck?! Call it!"

"Yeah, he's not happy," Michaels so astutely concluded.

Then, the Prime Video cameras panned to McCarthy, who appeared to say, "F*cking a**hole."

To be fair, the adrenaline of an NFL game lends itself to intense outbursts like this that wouldn't happen in any other setting and shouldn't necessarily be overblown. Just ask Andy Reid and Travis Kelce. But McCarthy and Rodgers have a complicated history, so any tension between those two particular guys is going to raise eyebrows.

McCarthy and Rodgers won a Super Bowl together during their 13-year tenure as head coach and quarterback, respectively, with the Green Bay Packers. They reportedly had an ugly falling out before the Packers fired McCarthy in December 2018.

In January, after NBC's newest media darling Mike Tomlin stepped down, the Steelers hired McCarthy as their new head coach. Rodgers signed a one-year contract in May, reuniting with McCarthy.

"The other aspect that I think is still a feeling out process is Rodgers and McCarthy are like that ex you ended up getting back together with after a long time," Jordan Rodgers, Aaron's brother, said on First Take last week. "You're like, 'Hey, things are better. We're different people. We're still trying to figure out those quirks that we had when we were in a relationship.' So, I think they're still trying to feel out who they want to be based on what they both are capable of in this second iteration of their relationship."

Rodgers, a four-time NFL MVP, has confirmed that this season will be his final NFL season. McCarthy just has to make this remarriage work for a few more months before Rodgers disappears from public life to start a family with his mysterious wife.

title: Pistons' Jalen Duren contract squabble over as he finally signs deal
description: After a contentious contract negotiation that saw Jalen Duren take meetings with other teams, he accepted the Detroit Pistons' offer on Thursday.
fullText:
It went until the buzzer, but the Detroit Pistons have finally reached an agreement with their biggest offseason free agent.

After a contentious contract negotiation that saw Jalen Duren take free agency meetings with other teams, and leaked reports about his purported desire to play elsewhere, the Pistons' second-best player last season is returning for 2026-27.

Duren and the Pistons agreed to a five-year, $200 million contract on Thursday, Oct. 1, keeping the All-NBA big with the Pistons, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

WELCOME BACK: Detroit Pistons ready to welcome Jalen Duren back – when deal is done

The 22-year-old had until 11:59 p.m. on Oct. 1 to take the qualifying offer, which was worth $9.6 million and would've allowed him to enter unrestricted free agency in 2027. Unsatisfied with the Pistons' offers this summer, Duren waited within hours of the deadline to accept the extension. He missed Monday's media day and the first three days of training camp, which started on Tuesday.

"He was a huge reason for our success these last two seasons. Had a tremendous season individually last year as well," president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said Monday.

"We believe he will do the same thing this year, upcoming and are excited to have him back when he gets back. We'll integrate him and he's going to have a fantastic season regardless of his decision. We look forward to getting him back."

Duren joins the organization with just a few days to reacclimate himself before preseason tips off against the Phoenix Suns on Monday (7 p.m., TV 20 - The Spot). He and the Pistons will now try to put a protracted negotiation behind them and build momentum entering the season.

"He knows how I feel about him and I continue to let him know how I feel about him, and that's really all that matters," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said Monday. "I love JD. I know how JD feels about me, how he feels about being a member of the Pistons. It's positive. I know there's a lot of things out there being said, but he's a huge part of what we do, he's a huge part of where we are right now, the steps that we've taken to get there. Comes to the work that he's put in, the effort and the sacrifices that he's made for this team and his teammates. It's all love from our standpoint and we look forward to having him back."

Duren's $40 million average annual value is second on the Pistons, behind only Cade Cunningham's $53.8 million per year on a five-year, $269 million rookie extension signed in July 2024. It also makes Duren the eighth highest-paid center in the NBA in annual value, ahead of Houston Rockets big man Alperen Sengun and Oklahoma City Thunder star Chet Holmgren.

Duren joins Ausar Thompson as the newest Pistons to have their futures locked in. Thompson signed a five-year, $155 million rookie extension that kicks in after this season, and is projected to eat up around 16% of the salary cap annually.

Duren entered restricted free agency after a breakout third-team All-NBA season, followed by a poor playoff performance in two series.

With the two sides far apart in contract talks, Duren took free agency meetings with the Sacramento Kings and Los Angeles Lakers, but his leverage dried up quickly.

Duren stays with the franchise that drafted him No. 13 overall out of Memphis in 2022.

Duren averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game over 28.2 minute in 70 games, all starts, on 65% shooting with two assists to 1.9 turnovers, 0.8 steals and 0.8 blocks for a 60-win Pistons team that lost in Game 7 to Cleveland in the second round last season.

He played a key role in helping the Pistons lock down the Eastern Conference 1-seed despite Cunningham's collapsed long in mid-March, and scored 22.6 points per game after the All-Star break.

For his four-year NBA career in the regular season, Duren has averaged 13.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, 2.1 assists to 1.8 turnovers, 0.7 steals and 0.9 blocks in 276 games (239 starts) over 27 minutes per game.

MEET THE ROOK: How Ebuka Okorie made rapid rise from 3-star recruit to 1st-round pick

Duren earned All-NBA third-team honors in 2025-26, qualifying him for a contract worth up to $287 million that starts at 30% of the salary cap with 8% raises.

Though the final tally on Duren's new deal fell well short of that max, it commits him to a team that emerged as a contender last season thanks to him and Cunningham, his fellow All-NBA point guard.

Despite reporting that his camp would push for sign-and-trade offers after the Pistons' initial offerings fell short, the Pistons never wanted to engage in a trade.

The Pistons repeatedly have signaled Duren, who will turn 23 in November, is a priority and one of their three core players they wish to build around, even after his numbers dropped significantly in 14 playoff games this past spring. Duren averaged just 10.2 points (9.3 fewer than his regular-season average, the second-biggest drop by an All-Star in NBA history), 8.5 rebounds, 2.1 assists to 2.3 turnovers, and 1.2 blocks on 51.4% shooting in 30.1 minutes per game. He was outplayed in the playoffs by third-string center Paul Reed.

Duren, who is from a Philadelphia suburb, fared much better in his first playoffs in 2025, a six-game first-round series loss to the New York Knicks in which he collected 11.8 points on 65% shooting with 10.7 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.7 blocks in 33.8 minutes.

Here's the Pistons' new-look center depth chart entering the 2026-27 season:

Jalen Duren, Paul Reed, Tolu Smith, Ugonna Onyenso (two-way contract),

The Pistons traded backup center Isaiah Stewart to the Memphis Grizzlies on June 24 during the NBA Draft, and traded into the second round to draft Virginia center Ugonna Onyenso and signed him to a two-way contract.

Reed, who is on an expiring $5.6 million nonguaranteed deal for 2026-27 projects as the backup to Duren. The Pistons also picked up a $2.4 million team option on 25-year-old Tolu Smith, who was converted from a two-way contract in April.

Duren will have a new power forward next to him with the Pistons acquiring John Collins in free agency and letting Tobias Harris, their No. 2 scorer in the playoffs, go to the San Antonio Spurs.

Duren was drafted by then-Pistons general manager Troy Weaver in 2022 at No. 13 overall. Duren, the youngest prospect in that draft, played one season in college at Memphis. The Pistons acquired Duren in a three-team deal with the Charlotte Hornets and New York Knicks. The Pistons sent the Milwaukee Bucks' 2025 top-four protected first-round pick (which they acquired from Portland in the Jerami Grant trade one day prior) to the Knicks, and took on Kemba Walker's salary.

Duren, 22 years old, was born Nov. 18, 2003, and grew up in New Castle, Delaware. He turns 23 on Nov. 18, 2026.

Duren is listed at 6 feet 10, 250 pounds with a 7-5 wingspan.

title: Jalen Duren Makes Final Decision on $200 Million Pistons Offer
description: Jalen Duren has agreed to a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract with the Detroit Pistons, ending a prolonged restricted free-agency dispute.
fullText:
The standoff is over. Jalen Duren is staying with the Detroit Pistons.

Duren has agreed to sign a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to Detroit, agent Chafie Fields told ESPN's Shams Charania on Thursday night. The agreement ends a restricted free-agency battle that stretched through the summer, Media Day and into the opening days of Pistons training camp.

The timing could hardly have been more dramatic. Earlier Thursday, Detroit was preparing for three possible outcomes before the deadline, including Duren accepting his $9.6 million qualifying offer and potentially reaching unrestricted free agency next summer.

Instead, Detroit got the outcome it had been chasing for months: its All-NBA center back on a long-term contract.

Getting here was anything but smooth. Negotiations deteriorated badly enough that Duren skipped Media Day and was absent when Detroit opened training camp, while reports indicated that his frustration extended beyond the dollars involved.

Detroit's offer had previously included weight-related provisions, another source of tension between the sides. The Pistons eventually removed the weight clause from their $200 million proposal, leaving Duren with a much cleaner choice between long-term security and a one-year bet on himself.

The latter would have been an extraordinary gamble. Under NBA restricted-free-agency rules, signing the qualifying offer would have put Duren under contract for one season, while the Pistons' long-term proposal offered $200 million in guaranteed money immediately.

Duren chose security, and Detroit chose continuity.

The size of the investment makes considerably more sense when viewed through what Duren accomplished last season. He averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds, earned his first All-Star selection and was named third-team All-NBA while helping Detroit produce its best season in two decades.

There were legitimate questions coming out of the postseason, when Duren's production declined during Detroit's second-round loss to Cleveland. Those concerns helped make the $200 million decision complicated, but they did not erase the reality that Detroit had a 22-year-old All-NBA center entering what should be the prime developmental years of his career.

The agreement also removes a potentially massive distraction for a team with championship ambitions. Duren had been absent from Detroit's official training camp roster, leaving J.B. Bickerstaff to begin preparing for the season without his starting center.

Now Bickerstaff can start putting the actual team together.

Detroit's decision also clarifies the franchise's long-term construction around Cade Cunningham. Rather than risk losing Duren next summer or allowing the contract battle to linger deeper into the season, the Pistons now have another foundational player secured through multiple seasons.

President of basketball operations Trajan Langdon had maintained publicly that Detroit would welcome Duren back regardless of how contentious negotiations became. At Media Day, Langdon said Duren would remain a major part of the team and emphasized that the organization intended to get the best version of him once the situation was resolved.

The Pistons committed $200 million to a center who won't turn 23 until November. Duren, meanwhile, chose the organization that drafted him rather than risking a guaranteed fortune for the possibility of something larger next summer.

After months of offers, counterpressure, missed team activities and increasingly uncomfortable headlines, none of that matters nearly as much now.

Jalen Duren is a Detroit Piston for the long haul.

title: Reviewing the Bears’ PFN grades from Week 3 vs. Eagles
description: After the Bears’ win over the Eagles, we look at how PFN scored each of Chicago’s starters in Week 3.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears bounced back in a major way on Monday night, picking up the decisive 27-7 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles to improve to 2-1 for the season.

It was about as thorough a beating as one could imagine. The Bears' passing attack proved to be too much for the Eagles to overcome, while Chicago's heavy blitz helped them generate pressure on passing downs and keep Jalen Hurts guessing all evening. These efforts are reflected in the analytics, where several key contributors on the Bears finished with favorable production.

Each week, I'll review how Chicago's eligible performers graded by Pro Football Network's Impact Scoring model. Here's how Week 3 looked.

Case Keenum: 79.1 (12th of 32 QBs)

Jonah Jackson: 77.3 (21st of 60 OGs)

Darnell Wright: 85.7 (1st of 71 OTs)

Week 3 marked the second week in a row that Darnell Wright finished with the highest PFN OL Impact grade of any offensive tackle in the NFL. He remains the top-graded lineman in the league, regardless of position. Keenum was quite efficient with his workload, ranking No. 12 in the NFL with 0.18 EPA per dropback. Though he finished the game with a strong 70.6% completion percentage, his completion percentage over expected (CPOE) was just +2.8. Jaylon Johnson: 67.5 (81st of 92 CBs)

After a stellar outing in Week 3, Dillon Thieneman now ranks as the second-best safety in the NFL by PFN SAF Impact grading to start the year. Against Philadelphia, he allowed a targeted passer rating of just 2.8 in coverage, with his key interception of Andy Dalton in the end zone playing a major factor in the Bears' win. Elsewhere in the secondary, Jaylon Johnson remains an analytical liability. However, both Devin Bush and T.J. Edwards have graded above average in coverage at the linebacker position.

title: Pro-Palestinian Protest Disrupts Ireland Soccer Match
description: Pro-Palestinian Protest Disrupts Ireland Soccer Match
fullText:
Protesters opposed to Ireland playing its Nations League soccer matches against Israel tossed tennis balls onto the pitch Thursday during Ireland's 2-2 draw against Austria at Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

Ireland was leading 1-0 after 19 minutes when about 30 tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text "#StopTheGame" were thrown onto the pitch. Referee Allard Lindhout took the players to the sideline while the balls were cleared, drawing boos from the crowd, the Irish Times reported.

"I think it kind of helped us in a good moment," Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told Irish broadcaster RTE of the protest, according to The Times of Israel.

"We could have a breather and some drinks. But you're never happy with this, but understand it and respect it."

The game resumed after a four-minute break, but there was another brief delay about 15 minutes later when a man carrying a Palestinian flag ran onto the pitch before being stopped by security.

At halftime, RTE published a statement in which the "Stop the Game" initiative claimed responsibility for throwing the tennis balls and declared the protest over.

"It was a token act, ‌deliberately limited, ⁠but necessary and done in solidarity with Gavin Bazunu and the people of Palestine facing genocide," the statement said.

Bazunu, an Ireland goalkeeper, withdrew from the squad for its two matches against Israel, saying he believed "it would be wrong to participate." Ireland's players held lengthy discussions over whether to play Sunday's first match against Israel before a "significant majority" voted to proceed.

Ireland defeated Israel 3-0 in Debrecen, Hungary. The Irish players wore black armbands and did not shake hands with their Israeli counterparts before the match.

In June, the Football Association of Ireland moved Sunday's second game against Israel to a neutral venue in Serbia, citing "operational challenges" that could affect staging the game in Ireland. The match will be played behind closed doors.

The move followed the FAI's own motion in November 2025 calling on UEFA, European soccer's governing body, to suspend Israel from club and international competitions.

The "Stop the Game" initiative issued an open letter Wednesday urging the Irish team and Hallgrimsson not to play Sunday and has called on the Irish government and FAI to cancel the game.

Ireland has been one of the most vocal critics of Israel's conduct of the war in Gaza following Iranian-backed Hamas' terrorist attack on Oct. 7, 2023. Dublin formally recognized a Palestinian state in 2024 alongside Spain and Norway.

Israel closed its embassy in Dublin later that year, accusing the Irish government of extreme anti-Israel policies and antisemitism.

Ireland's exhibition match against Qatar at Aviva Stadium in May also was halted twice when protesters threw tennis balls onto the pitch to protest the scheduled matches against Israel.

title: “It Wasn’t an Infraction”: 49ers’ Kyle Juszczyk Calls Out NFL’s Beer Endorsements After Hefty Fine for Controversial Celebration
description: Kyle Juszczyk has been celebrating on the field with a juice-chugging action for ages. However, things didn’t sit well this time, as the NFL took it as a beer chug imitation after he celebrated a touchdown pass in the game against the Miami Dolphins.
fullText:
Kyle Juszczyk has been celebrating on the field with a juice-chugging action for ages. However, things didn't sit well this time, as the NFL took it as a beer chug imitation after he celebrated a touchdown pass in the game against the Miami Dolphins. And all he did was take his right hand up to his mouth, tilt his head, and pretend to drink from the imaginary bottle.

The NFL put a $14,926 penalty on Juszczyk for the action. The San Francisco 49ers' fullback has been arguing that it was juice, not beer, in his actions. Juszczyk recently claimed that even if it was beer, the league shouldn't have put a fine on him.

"Even if it was beer, I don't think that should be a problem with all of the beer endorsements that we have in the NFL," Juszczyk told the media during a locker room interview. "We have the Bud Light Celly Can, the Bud Light Porch… We have everything. So, even if it was beer, which it wasn't, I still felt like it wasn't an infraction."

Back on December 20, 2021, Anheuser-Busch InBev, the brand behind Budweiser, signed a multi-year renewal as the global exclusive beer and hard seltzer sponsor for the league. The extension will last through the 2026-27 season.

Juszczyk further defended his case during his appearance on Jason and Travis Kelce's New Heights Podcast.

"So my nickname for the longest time has been Juice," the fullback said on the Kelce brothers' podcast. "I have literally a juice box on my thigh pad. The whole stadium yells juice when I touch the ball. So, a homage to that is literally I drink juice. And that's been going down for the longest time."

However, Travis Kelce wasn't too convinced. He claimed that the way Juszczyk did it, it looked like beer and not juice. He argued that people don't usually do a "full chug on a juice." But that invited another call for hypocrisy from the 49ers fullback.

"You can't drink juice when you got the Bud Light patio in the end zone. When you're cutting through the Bud Light celly can. It's a hypocrisy, man."

Juszczyk also noted that the NFL didn't really have to put that big of a fine on him just to make him stop doing something. He claimed that he would have stopped his celebrations had the league asked him to stop. And later, Juszczyk claimed that he doesn't drink beer.

"I don't even really drink beer," he said. "I drink maybe five times a year in the offseason, but I started thinking about it and there are two common denominators of when I do drink alcohol. One of them I was at Bandon Dunes with Travis and George. I was at Tight End U with Travis and George. And I was at Travis' wedding with Travis and George."

ESPN's Nick Wagner reported on X that Juszczyk appeared in court Tuesday to appeal the fine for "chugging a beer." As of October 1, Juszczyk is awaiting the court's decision on his appeal. However, Juszczyk believes that things will work out. Even Wagner claimed that good things will come for the 49ers fullback out of the whole situation.

Juszczyk isn't the only one facing the fines. Indianapolis Colts guard Matt Goncalves received an $8,847 fine, and the Dallas Cowboys tight end Jake Ferguson got a $13,611 fine for mimicking the consumption of a beverage that many assumed to be beer.

The NFL's decision to fine Kyle Juszczyk for drinking an imaginary beverage while heavily promoting massive beer endorsements made the fullback call out the hypocrisy. But for now, all he needs to do is wait for the court to respond to his appeal.

title: St. Edward’s completes reverse sweep, beats Pine School in Class 1A showdown
description: Pine School and St. Edward's clashed Thursday in a volleyball postseason tuneup just over a week before district tournaments are scheduled to begin.
fullText:
HOBE SOUND — Behind the guidance of first-year head coaches, St. Edward's and Pine School are ranked among the top girls volleyball teams in Class 1A as the regular season nears its conclusion.

The two teams clashed Thursday in a postseason tuneup just over a week before district tournaments are scheduled to begin. While the Knights came out strong, it was the Pirates who left "The Dungeon" with the last laugh.

St. Edward's rallied from an 0-2 deficit to complete a reverse sweep and claim a five-set victory. Set scores were 18-25, 21-25, 25-20, 25-11, 15-9 on Thursday night at Pine School.

"We've been practicing all season on mental toughness and being disciplined and consistent. The timeouts during the match were just reminders that this is what we've been training for all year," St. Edward's head coach Kelsey Fox said. "Really, having them come together and push for that is all on them. They put in the work."

Fox credited improved communication among her players for the comeback. The visitors avoided the sweep by pulling away late in the third set before using two 7-1 runs to breeze through the fourth.

A kill by freshman outside hitter Vitoria Claret and a block by junior Bodhi Lindley tied the deciding set at 5-5. St. Edward's then scored seven of the next eight points, recording aces from sophomores Grace Clemente and Alexandra Jefferson while capitalizing on several Pine mistakes. The Knights committed two service errors, two net violations and a hitting error during that stretch.

"We started strong, but if you get lackadaisical, you're giving another team a chance to take over," Pine School head coach Kendall Holmes said. "That team did a great job of making adjustments against us, and we didn't do as great a job responding to that. It's a lesson for them, so that's great, but it's definitely something we need to work on."

A kill by Violet Clemente sealed the Pirates' fifth win in their past six matches. The eighth grader finished with 12 kills, matching junior Nevin Waddell. Grace Clemente led the Pirates with 14 kills. The trio also contributed three aces apiece.

title: ‘The Plan Is To Knock Him Out’ – Tonglampoon, Dionatha Santos Tobias Trade Words Ahead Of ONE Friday Fights 173
description: Speed meets pressure as two seasoned strawweights reveal very different plans for their small-gloves showdown.
fullText:
Tonglampoon FA Group and Dionatha Santos Tobias both see clear paths to a devastating finish when they collide in an explosive strawweight Muay Thai showdown.

The dangerous strikers square off in the main event of ONE Friday Fights 173 on Friday, October 2, broadcasting live in Asia primetime from Bangkok's iconic Lumpinee Stadium.

Tonglampoon brings a seasoned 48-15 professional record into his 11th appearance on the weekly series. The 22-year-old Thai standout has already produced a lengthy collection of memorable battles and notable victories under the ONE Championship banner.

Santos Tobias, meanwhile, has showcased serious finishing ability whenever he has found success in the world's largest martial arts organization. Both of the Brazilian's promotional victories have come by way of knockout, including a body-shot finish of Mahahin Petkiatpet and a first-round stoppage of Kongpoxay PK Saenchai.

Now, he intends to use his blistering speed and precision to test a specific vulnerability he sees in Tonglampoon, while the Thai standout plans to answer by turning one of the Brazilian's favorite weapons directly against him.

Tonglampoon has approached this main event matchup with plenty of profound self-reflection.

The FA Group representative firmly believes hesitation has cost him dearly in previous appearances, so his latest camp has centered entirely on tightening his defense while making sure he gets to work immediately rather than waiting for the action to come to him.

His hands and elbows have been particular areas of emphasis.

"I've been focusing heavily on training hard, improving my defense, and engaging straight away instead of hesitating or waiting.

"I believe that hesitation was what led to me getting knocked out in previous fights. This time, I want to get straight to work, and I've been sharpening my hands and elbows."

The adjustments have not been purely technical. Tonglampoon also spent valuable time away from the gym reflecting on what had gone wrong, actively trying to rebuild his confidence before another high-profile assignment at Lumpinee Stadium.

Time alone in nature gave him the necessary space to reset, while the people closest to him helped restore his competitive motivation.

"I spent some time alone back home and went into nature to reflect on what happened.

"Being somewhere quiet helped me find peace, and the support from my family and friends gave me the motivation to stand up again."

That renewed mindset will be tested immediately by an opponent known for marching forward and investing heavily in body attacks.

But Tonglampoon has absolutely no intention of simply absorbing Santos Tobias' pressure. He believes the Brazilian can be hurt to the body as well and wants to force him into the exact kind of toe-to-toe exchanges he normally imposes on others.

"That's exactly why I want to bring my elbows into play against Dionatha. I also think he can be vulnerable to body shots.

"I want to see if his body can handle my power. I'm going to pressure him, target the body, stand toe-to-toe, and attack him with the same body pressure he likes to put on his opponents. For this fight, my focus is heavily on my boxing."

Dionatha Santos Tobias respects the vast experience and sheer toughness that Tonglampoon brings into their three-round battle.

The 26-year-old has identified strong punches and kicks in the Thai fighter's arsenal, but he does not believe durability alone will be enough to decide the contest.

"He's very tough. He has a very good left-right kick to the leg, good punches, and everything.

"But he's just very tough, you know? Just being tough doesn't win anything. Being tough doesn't win everything. You have to have more."

Santos Tobias believes his greatest advantage could come from his ability to adapt once the action begins.

Rather than relying on one predetermined combination, the Sangmorakot representative wants several tactical answers ready depending on what Tonglampoon presents under ONE's small-gloves Muay Thai rules. Speed and precision, however, remain central to his overarching plan.

"I could say a lot of things, but to be honest, to beat someone, especially in a small-gloves fight, depends on how you feel in the moment.

"I am a guy who has something prepared, but if that one doesn't work, I have another thing, and then another thing. It depends on how I play chess. I'm going to take advantage of how much faster I am than him, quicker than him, and how my hands are more precise than his."

The Brazilian has also studied Tonglampoon's recent performances closely enough to identify one particular target.

Asked about his opponent's weaknesses, Santos Tobias immediately pointed to his chin.

And while his own body punching has already produced a spectacular knockout, he suspects Tonglampoon may be expecting him to heavily attack downstairs again. That could easily open other possibilities as Dionatha hunts for his third victory in the promotion.

"In his last couple of fights, the chin was the problem, so maybe. And I'm sure that he thinks I'm going to punch only the body instead.

"The plan is to knock him out, but if this doesn't work, I'm happy if I win."

title: Jalen Duren ends standoff with Pistons, agrees to $200 million contract
description: Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren finally has a new contract. Duren had a breakout season in 2025-26, earning an All-Star nod.
fullText:
The saga between the Detroit Pistons and Jalen Duren has finally ended as the disgruntled center agreed to a new five-year, $200 million contract to return to Detroit, according to multiple reports.

The agreement came in ahead of Thursday's 11:59 p.m. ET deadline to decide on a $9.62 million qualifying offer.

Duren averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds in 70 games in 2025-26 and was named an All-Star for the first time in his four-year career.

After being named to the All-NBA third team, Duren was eligible to sign a five-year deal, worth up to around $287 million, or 30% of the salary cap.

But Duren's dreadful playoff performance made any team, especially the Pistons, reluctant to pay that much. Duren's per-game production dipped to 10.2 points, 8.5 rebounds and 1.2 blocks on 51.4% shooting. The top-seeded Pistons were eliminated in the second round in seven games by the Cleveland Cavaliers.

The Pistons had maintained they were not going to trade Duren, as few teams had the salary cap space available to take on the maximum contract Duren was seeking. He did not get the max, but is now set to make $200 million over the next five seasons.

Duren became a restricted free agent this offseason upon completion of his four-year, $19.4 million rookie-scale contract. He could have become an unrestricted free agent next summer if he had accepted the $9.62 million qualifying offer from Detroit.

Agreeing to a five-year, $200 million deal, Duren is slated to be on the Pistons for the forseeable future.

Duren is 22 years old. He was drafted by the Charlotte Hornets with the 13th overall pick in the 2022 NBA Draft after one season of college ball at Memphis. Duren was traded to Detroit in a three-way draft-night deal that also involved the New York Knicks.

In four NBA seasons, Duren has averaged 13.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 2.1 assists per game, while shooting 65% from the field. During the 2025-26 season, Duren averaged a career-high 19.5 points, along with 10.5 rebounds, 2.0 assists and shot 65% from the field.

title: What Went Wrong for the Astros in Wild Card Loss
description: The Houston Astros' postseason is over after being swept by the Chicago White Sox in the American League Wild Card Series. Houston dropped Game 1 by a score of 6-3 before falling 7-3 in Game 2, ending its postseason hopes after just two games. What went wrong? How the Astros Postseason Ended So Quickly …
fullText:
The Houston Astros' postseason is over after being swept by the Chicago White Sox in the American League Wild Card Series. Houston dropped Game 1 by a score of 6-3 before falling 7-3 in Game 2, ending its postseason hopes after just two games. What went wrong?

Astros ace Hunter Brown was supposed to be the guy who saved the team. After Houston dropped game one, the Astros had their ace on the mound with the season on the line. Brown finished the regular season with a 3.19 ERA and had dominated the White Sox earlier in the season, allowing no runs over seven innings in a July matchup. Instead, Brown couldn't even make it out of the first inning.

The White Sox sent nine batters to the plate against him and scored four runs before manager Joe Espada had to make the call to the bullpen. Brown gave up five hits, walked one, and was charged with four runs, three of them earned, while throwing 36 pitches. The defense certainly didn't help him, but Brown was supposed to be the Astros' ace, and he needed to find a way to limit the damage. He didn't.

Hunter Brown doesn’t make it out of the first inning:

0.2 IP, 5 H, 4 R, 3 ER, 1 BB, 2 SO, 36 P pic.twitter.com/DMU3sW6FXq

— Talkin’ Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) September 30, 2026

The biggest problem was the timing. Houston had already used eight pitchers in its Game 1 bullpen game, meaning the Astros needed Brown to provide length in Game 2. Instead, they had to go to the bullpen before the first inning was even over. That put even more pressure on a pitching staff that was already being stretched thin. At the risk of stating the obvious, the Astros simply did not pitch well enough to win this series.

The Astros' offense showed flashes of life, but it never came close to being consistent enough. Houston had opportunities in both games and failed to capitalize on enough of them.

In Game 1, the Astros managed only six hits and went 0-for-7 with runners in scoring position. That became especially costly because Chicago's pitching staff was constantly changing looks and keeping Houston's hitters uncomfortable. Game 2 followed a similar script. Jeremy Peña hit a leadoff home run in the first inning, and Cam Smith and Jose Altuve later hit solo homers of their own. Suddenly, a game that looked like it could get out of hand was 4-3.

That was the moment for the Astros to make something happen. Instead, Houston couldn't finish the comeback. The Astros loaded the bases with one out in the fifth inning, but likely AL MVP Yordan Alvarez lined out, and Altuve followed with a flyout to end the threat. Chicago responded with Chase Meidroth's three-run homer in the sixth. That was the ballgame.

Jose Altuve flies out with the bases loaded to end the inning https://t.co/Wlnp0KQxv4 pic.twitter.com/STRgEGG71r

— Talkin’ Baseball (@TalkinBaseball_) September 30, 2026

The Astros' biggest problem wasn't a lack of opportunities. It was their inability to consistently turn those opportunities into runs when they mattered most.

Then there was the situation with the fans. Astros fans booed their team during Game 1 as Houston fell behind early, and some Astros players were openly unhappy with the reaction. Bennett Sousa and Christian Walker were among the players who spoke out about the boos, with Walker saying the team wanted the support of the home crowd. Sousa also expressed frustration with the reaction. That quickly became a bigger story than it probably needed to be.

Houston pitcher Bennett Sousa didn’t appreciate boos from Astros fans during their Wild Card opener vs. Chicago 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/9S7I8ppi58

— Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) September 30, 2026

The Astros had just lost the opening game of a playoff series while getting outplayed for most of the afternoon. The frustration from the crowd was understandable, even if the players obviously didn't appreciate it. Espada took a more measured approach. The Astros manager said he understood both sides and emphasized that Houston needed its fans and fed off their energy.

Still, the fact that players were talking about the crowd after a playoff loss was not ideal. The Astros had bigger problems to worry about. They were one loss away from going home.

The Astros' postseason ended much earlier than they wanted, and the offseason could be an interesting one in Houston. General manager Dana Brown was dismissed in late August, and Espada's contract expires after the season with no extension in place, according to the Houston Chronicle. Those questions will dominate the offseason. For now, though, the biggest takeaway from the Houston Astros' Wild Card loss to the White Sox is pretty simple.

They didn't pitch well enough. They didn't hit well enough in the biggest moments. And once things started going wrong, the Astros never really found a way to stop the bleeding. For a team that fought all season just to get back to October, getting swept in two games is a brutal way for the season to end. Houston will have to figure out why before they get another chance.

title: Ex-hockey coach spots ‘eerie’ Connor McDavid similarities in Sharks’ Macklin Celebrini
description: Drew Remenda compares Macklin Celebrini’s work ethic and habits to Connor McDavid.
fullText:
Former hockey coach Drew Remenda sees striking similarities between Connor McDavid and San Jose Sharks captain Macklin Celebrini.

Speaking on The Sheet with Jeff Marek, Remenda compared the two NHL stars' habits, work ethic and approach to hockey.

"Connor practices at full speed all the time. All the time," Remenda said. "And Connor's never happy with his game. He always thinks that he could have done more."

MORE: Oilers trading for Connor Hellebuyck is a 'long shot' but not 'impossible,' per NHL analyst

Remenda then made the comparison even clearer.

"By describing Connor like that, I'm describing Macklin Celebrini," he said. "Guys, it's eerie how many of the same characteristics they have."

Celebrini has quickly become the centerpiece of San Jose's rebuild. The 20-year-old was named the youngest captain in Sharks history before the 2026-27 season.

Remenda said Celebrini's preparation particularly reminds him of McDavid. He pointed to the Sharks forward arriving early for morning skate and continuing to work after teammates leave.

"Morning skate, goalies are out, here comes Macklin," Remenda said. "Macklin's out there first, almost all the time. Smith comes out after him, they work on their shots, and then they act like children, like they are.

"I mean that in the greatest way possible. Macklin stays out. Macklin's work ethic is ridiculous."

Chicago, Illinois, USA; San Jose Sharks center Macklin Celebrini (71) warms up at United Center. Mandatory Credit: David Banks-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Remenda believes Celebrini has handled the media side of his career differently than McDavid did early on.

"One thing that Macklin does a little bit better than Connor at this stage in his career is Macklin's been working on the PR side of it," Remenda said.

He added that Celebrini dislikes discussing himself, despite being increasingly comfortable with interviews and public attention. The biggest difference, however, comes from the pressure surrounding each player.

McDavid entered the NHL as the first overall pick and immediately carried enormous expectations in Edmonton. Celebrini also arrived as a first overall selection, but Remenda believes his environment allows more freedom.

"Connor's had so much pressure on him, and especially in that market, in Canada, everything's on him," Remenda said. "Mack doesn't have that peripheral opponent pressure, you know what I mean? It's easier in our room than it has been for Connor to be in his room."

MORE: Wayne Gretzky gives honest take on Connor McDavid's future with Oilers

That difference allows Celebrini to enjoy his rise more freely, according to Remenda.

"You see more joy in Macklin," he said. "Here, Macklin gets to enjoy that a little bit more."

Celebrini enters the season after recording 115 points last year. His development will now be closely watched as he takes on greater responsibility as San Jose's captain.

title: Pistons' Jalen Duren makes final decision on $200M contract offer ending months-long dispute
description: The Detroit and Jalen Duren have been going back and forth for most of the summer. The two sides have finally agreed on a new contract.
fullText:
Pistons' Jalen Duren makes final decision on $200M contract offer ending months-long dispute originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Detroit Pistons and Jalen Duren have been throwing jabs at each other throughout the entire summer. Most of the time, it felt like Duren wanted to be done with Detroit as the organization refused to give him the contract he wanted.

On Monday, the Pistons had media day, and the All-Star center did not show up after declining the offer.

Duren had been threatening to take the qualifying offer throughout the summer, saying that if the organization didn't meet his demands, he would commit to it. Detroit had an offer of $200 million on the table, but Duren wouldn't agree to it due to a weight clause. On Wednesday, it was removed as a last-second effort from the organization.

"Per league sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity as negotiations continue, the weight clause initially proposed as part of the Pistons' five-year, $200 million offer is no longer part of the talks. The clause was never put in writing," The Athletic's Sam Amick wrote.

With the qualifying offer deadline coming to a close on Thursday night, ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Duren had accepted the offer from the Pistons.

"All-NBA and All-Star center Jalen Duren has agreed to sign a five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed contract to return to the Detroit Pistons, agent Chafie Fields of THE•TEAM tells ESPN. This ends a prolonged restricted free agency dispute between the two sides," Charania posted.

Finally, the months-long dispute is over for Duren and the organization. The two sides finally came together when they needed to the most, but this doesn't necessarily mean the relationship is fixed.

That will be something to monitor as the season goes on. Duren will join the team in training camp sometime soon, with the first preseason game on Monday. At the very least, Detroit was able to get a deal done with the center they have wanted all summer, never turning on him no matter the circumstances.

title: Grok reportedly encouraged the capture of Venezuela's president
description: President Trump reportedly asked for Grok's opinion before invading Venezuela and capturing Nicolás Maduro.
fullText:
In December 2025, about a month before the U.S. invaded Venezuela and captured its president, Nicolás Maduro, President Trump had a secret meeting with Elon Musk, Time magazine reports. This was roughly seven months after Musk left his role in the Trump administration at the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).

During this meeting, Trump “spent hours” talking to Musk’s Grok chatbot, including asking how Venezuelans would respond to the capture of their president, a source told Time. Just a few months earlier, in September, Trump began ordering U.S. military strikes against Venezuelan boats that Trump alleged were involved in drug trafficking.

People had apparently been turning to Grok asking about the boat strikes and political climate in Venezuela, as The Atlantic reported at the time. So Grok told Trump that Maduro was a “deeply unpopular dictator and that many Venezuelans would likely celebrate his downfall,” Time reported.

When such celebrations indeed happened after the U.S. invaded on January 3, Trump apparently “came away thinking Grok was ingenious,” that source told Time.

So perhaps it should come as no surprise that in June of this year, the Pentagon’s head of AI said that the military used Gov Grok to deploy and strike targets during the Iran War.

While Grok isn’t the only AI model serving the DoD (OpenAI also has an agreement and Anthropic has been in a back-and-forth over how its models can be used for military intelligence and in modern warfare), Grok may become an even bigger favorite under this administration. Earlier this week, the Pentagon announced that Musk and Anduril’s Palmer Luckey have been tapped to co-lead a study about how advanced technology is, and can be, used in battlefields.

title: Creatine may help build muscle even without exercise, researchers find
description: Creatine helped middle-aged adults gain muscle and strength even without a structured workout program in a new 12-week study. When combined with exercise and a calorie-reduced diet, it produced even greater strength gains while helping participants add lean tissue and lose fat. Researchers say the results strengthen the case for creatine as a potentially useful tool for maintaining muscle with age.
fullText:
Creatine is widely known for helping support muscle growth and athletic performance, but researchers are increasingly examining whether its benefits extend well beyond the gym. New findings from Texas A&M University suggest creatine may be particularly useful in middle age, when preserving muscle becomes increasingly important.

In a 12-week study published in the Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition, adults ages 45 to 65 who took creatine increased their lean tissue and strength even if they did not follow a structured exercise program. Participants who combined creatine with regular exercise experienced even larger improvements.

The results add to growing research exploring creatine as more than a supplement for athletes. Scientists are also studying whether it can help support muscle health and healthy aging.

The study was led by Dr. Richard Kreider, professor and director of the Exercise and Sport Nutrition Lab at Texas A&M. Kreider has studied creatine for more than three decades. Creatine occurs naturally in the body and helps restore cellular energy, and decades of research have examined its effects on exercise performance, muscle growth, and strength. Kreider's earlier work has also suggested that creatine may offer health benefits throughout life.

Creatine Benefits Without Structured Exercise

The new study involved 64 healthy adults who completed the full 12-week intervention. Participants decided whether to join a structured exercise and diet-induced weight-loss program or remain in a non-exercise group. Within those groups, they were randomly assigned to consume either 10 grams of creatine monohydrate or a placebo each day.

Among participants who did not join the exercise program, those taking creatine gained roughly 2.4 pounds of lean tissue over the 12 weeks. They also increased their leg press and bench press strength.

Participants in the exercise program performed both resistance and aerobic training three times per week. Those who added creatine experienced greater gains in leg press strength, bench press strength, and time to exhaustion.

Creatine did not appear to improve aerobic capacity beyond the benefits of exercise alone. That result fits with previous evidence showing that creatine primarily supports muscular strength and power rather than aerobic fitness.

Building Muscle While Losing Fat

Researchers also examined another important issue: how to reduce body fat without losing muscle in the process.

Participants in the exercise group followed a diet that created a modest calorie deficit. After 12 weeks, those who took creatine had added nearly three pounds of lean tissue while also losing fat mass. By comparison, participants following the same exercise and diet program while taking a placebo showed little change in lean tissue.

The creatine group also experienced a larger decrease in body fat percentage. According to the researchers, this is the first study to show that adding creatine to an exercise and diet-induced weight-loss program can reduce body fat percentage more than exercise and diet alone.

The findings add to decades of research investigating creatine for purposes beyond athletic performance.

Kreider has previously emphasized creatine's importance throughout the lifespan, including its potential value for older adults facing age-related declines in muscle mass and cognitive function.

The body makes creatine naturally, and it is also found in foods including meat and fish. However, Kreider says many people do not consume enough through food alone. Reaching a daily intake of 10 grams from diet alone would require eating roughly five to 10 pounds of meat or fish each day, he notes, making supplements a more practical and less costly option.

Creatine is also among the most heavily studied sports and nutritional supplements. In a 2025 analysis, Kreider and his colleagues reviewed 685 clinical trials and found no significant difference in reported side-effect rates between people taking creatine and those receiving a placebo.

The study was funded by the WoodNext Foundation through the Texas A&M Foundation.

Website: https://wileai.github.io/pi-codex-connectors/

The model gets three tools instead of hundreds of schemas:

/codex-connectors [refresh] shows the catalog.

Tools not annotated read-only need approval. PI_CODEX_CONNECTORS_WRITES:

Requires Node.js 22.19+ and Pi. This package is a Pi extension, not a standalone MCP server; other harnesses must support loading Pi extensions.

Alternatively, add the package to the existing packages array in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json (personal) or .pi/settings.json (project):

Project settings require Pi project trust. Restart Pi after installation or updating.

Keep the npm source unversioned to receive stable updates. An explicit version such as npm:@wileai/pi-codex-connector@0.1.1 stays pinned. Releases become available through npm; users choose when to update.

The package is now @wileai/pi-codex-connector. Existing installs of the old name need a one-time migration:

Use --local on both commands for a project-local installation. Restart Pi afterward. Future updates use pi update npm:@wileai/pi-codex-connector.

PI_CODEX_CONNECTORS_CODEX overrides the Codex executable.

Integration and scenario tests only; they use the real Codex app-server and your Codex login. No model tokens: pi scenarios use a scripted model (integration/fixtures/scripted-model.ts).

Use a dedicated, minimally privileged account for public CI. Tests keep connector responses in memory, drain child-process diagnostics, and report fixed failure labels rather than account data. Do not upload raw Pi transcripts or Codex diagnostics. Pi scenarios allowlist GitHub and set an explicit write policy. The test runner uses the development Pi host patched by make setup; PI_BIN can override it.

Connector names, schemas and results enter the selected Pi model's context. Pi and the model provider may retain them. Codex owning credentials does not keep connector results within Codex.

Before discovery, the extension asks for session consent. Headless runs must explicitly set PI_CODEX_CONNECTORS_DATA=allow; deny blocks access. Concurrent discovery shares one consent prompt. Session changes close the previous connector process and require fresh consent. Consent covers the session, including model changes: use only trusted models throughout it.

Optionally restrict discovery and calls with PI_CODEX_CONNECTORS_ALLOW=GitHub (comma-separated exact connector names or IDs). An empty value exposes no connectors. Without this setting all enabled, callable connectors are eligible. Read-only annotations are provider hints, not an independent authorization boundary.

Write approvals reject arguments over 2000 characters rather than hiding fields. WRITES=allow explicitly bypasses approval; use it only in trusted automation. Destructive tools require write approval even if also marked read-only.

Large results are truncated in memory, never saved by this extension. Narrow queries or paginate to retrieve more. Existing files from older versions are not removed automatically.

App-server errors, startup diagnostics, tool-catalog errors, and failed tool responses withhold raw details because they can contain local configuration or private data. The extension discards stderr instead of retaining it. Check Codex or the connected app locally when troubleshooting; never paste raw diagnostics into a public issue. Successful connector responses still enter the selected model's context as described above.

The app-server protocol has no per-call cancellation method for connector calls. An abort, timeout or disconnect after dispatch reports an unknown outcome, not a cancelled action. Affected writes block further writes for the service lifetime, including refresh. Check the connected app before restarting the session; never automatically retry an uncertain write. This is not durable idempotency across restarts.

See RELEASING.md for initial npm setup and the release checklist. Publishing a GitHub release triggers .github/workflows/publish.yml: it checks the release version, typechecks, audits runtime dependencies, verifies the package contents, and publishes with provenance. Stable releases use npm's latest tag; prereleases use next.

The pi-package keyword and pi.extensions manifest make the published package eligible for the Pi package catalog. Catalog indexing is external and may lag publication.

The extension has no runtime import of Pi's SDK; Pi SDK peer dependencies are optional type contracts. Keep your separately installed Pi host patched. Development setup explicitly patches Pi's upstream shrinkwrapped brace-expansion to 5.0.12. make check verifies the actual resolved version, because the root lockfile audit alone can miss the upstream shrinkwrap. Re-run make setup after any clean install.
